problem.statement: The Channel Booster only runs inside the Grok UI fork: its CLI needs tsx and this repo's package.json, its AI engines lose the playbook once moved, a creator's data is spread over the code folder, and nothing installable contains it.
successCriteria: A packed channel-booster tarball installed into an empty folder runs with plain node, loads the whole playbook, and keeps one channel's data inside one workspace folder
The booster verifies on its own in a folder that holds only its own files, with no Grok UI code or config
Every command documented before this mission still works from the repo root with the same flags and environment variables
The Desk opens dark and Grok-style by default, with a light option, and its human gates still work in the artifact viewer

definitionOfDone.claim: The installed bin runs under plain node with a node shebang; tsx is not needed at runtime
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: channel-booster/scripts/package-smoke.mjs: npm pack, install the tarball into an empty temp folder, run node_modules/.bin/channel-booster help; a non-zero exit, empty help, a tsx shebang, or tsx in the installed tree falsifies

definitionOfDone.claim: The playbook is built in: the installed bin run from a folder outside the repo sends the same doctrine files and hash as the source CLI
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: package-smoke runs `ai ideas --dry-run` from the temp folder and compares the doctrine file list and hash with the source run; any difference, or a zero-file doctrine that does not throw, falsifies

definitionOfDone.claim: One workspace folder per channel: with a workspace, every file a command writes lands inside that folder
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: package-smoke runs init, scan (bundled example), idea add, package build --offline and rules compile inside a temp workspace and snapshots the temp parent and the installed package; any new or changed file outside the workspace falsifies

definitionOfDone.claim: Workflow stages run in-process; no child process or tsx is needed to run a booster stage, and stored `npm run booster -- ...` stage commands still run
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: runner tests stub child_process to throw and still complete a command stage; a stored legacy-prefixed stage command runs to the same result

definitionOfDone.claim: Old runbooks still work: --data, --path, --root, --inbox, --playbook, BOOSTER_DATA and BOOSTER_PROFILE resolve exactly as before when no workspace is given
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: the full existing test suite fails, or the legacy-resolution tests in src/workspace.test.ts show a location different from the pre-mission default

definitionOfDone.claim: The booster verifies standalone in the layout the private repo will use
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: channel-booster/scripts/standalone-check.mjs copies only the booster's files into a temp folder with the split template root, runs npm install and npm run verify there; a non-zero exit falsifies

definitionOfDone.claim: The Desk is dark and Grok-style by default in every host theme, offers a light option, and keeps its in-page gates, zero network requests and a 390px layout without horizontal scroll
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: channel-booster/scripts/desk-runtime.mjs drives the built Desk in Chromium (desktop, 390x844 phone, sandboxed artifact frame, host data-theme light and dark); a light default, a failed gate, a network request, a console error, horizontal overflow or a text contrast below 4.5:1 falsifies

definitionOfDone.claim: The booster lives in a private repo with its history, and every later change reaches main through the gates workflow
definitionOfDone.falsifiedBy: in the new repo, `git log -- channel-booster` has fewer commits than in Grok-UI-test at the split point, Grok UI paths exist, or a merged PR has no passing verify check

confidence.biggestRisk: The private repo cannot be created from this session, so the split waits on the owner; the in-process runner can also change stage output in ways the old subprocess tests did not pin.
confidence.nextAction: Land the seam contracts (workspace, io, doctrine, build info), then run the four cut-the-ties lanes and the Desk lane in parallel.

rejectedAlternatives.idea: Split into the new repo first, then cut the ties there
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The session cannot create repositories; cutting the ties first also follows the Blueprint's order and lets the split be rehearsed in a temp folder before it is real.

rejectedAlternatives.idea: Commit a generated doctrine module and keep it in sync with a test
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A person accepting a rule edits the playbook in place in the repo, which would fail the sync test on their machine; embedding at bundle time keeps one source of truth.

rejectedAlternatives.idea: Bundle zod and the Anthropic SDK into the bin
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Bundled dependencies disappear from npm audit; they stay declared runtime dependencies and external to the bundle.
